gallery.title: File:150830-F-OE991-123 (21310730902).jpg
gallery.artist: US Air Force from USA
gallery.description: An F-15C Eagle is transported across the DuPont Bridge near Tyndall Air Force Base, Fla., Aug. 30, 2015. The F-15 was transported to Haney Technical Center to be used to train future aircraft mechanics in their Aviation Academy. (U.S. Air Force photo/Airman 1st Class Dustin Mullen)

gallery.title: File:Building bare-base operations (14028519653).jpg
gallery.artist: US Air Force from USA
gallery.description: Senior Airman Axel Fiksman welds a crossbar onto a pole while building a fence during Silver Flag training April 17, 2014, at Tyndall Air Force Base, Fla. During the weeklong course, guardsmen from the 116th Civil Engineer Squadron along with 219 Airmen from multiple active-duty, Reserve and Air National Guard units trained on building and maintaining bare-base operations at a simulated forward-deployed location. Fiksman is a structures specialist with the 116th CES of the Georgia ANG at Robins Air Force Base, Ga. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Master Sgt. Roger Parsons/Released)

gallery.title: File:Decontamination (10677097754).jpg
gallery.artist: US Air Force from USA
gallery.description: As members of the 325th Bioenvironmental Engineering team exit the suspected simulated chemical laboratory, they proceed through a decontamination area on Tyndall Air Force Base, Fla. The exercise gave Airmen the opportunity to respond to an unknown threat as a total force team. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. Javier Cruz)

gallery.title: File:Game plan (10677298933).jpg
gallery.artist: US Air Force from USA
gallery.description: As day turned to night, first responders used any available light to illuminate their emergency response efforts until temporary lighting could be established on Tyndall Air Force Base, Fla. The exercise gave Airmen the opportunity to respond to an unknown threat as a total force team. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. Javier Cruz)

gallery.title: File:170311-Z-QX261-016 (32630196384).jpg
gallery.artist: S.C. Air National Guard
gallery.description: U.S. Air Force Master Sgt. Anthony King, Chief Master Sgt. Harold Nash and Tech. Sgt. Sherman Padgett, left to right, of the 169th Maintenance Group, discuss the discuss the distribution of GBU-24 Paveway III laser-guided bombs to fighter jets at Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida on Mar. 11, 2017. More than 200 Airmen from the 169th Fighter Wing, South Carolina Air National Guard are deployed for the Weapons Systems Evaluation Program (WSEP). The WSEP’s purpose is to evaluate a unit’s ability to effectively deliver munitions through all stages, from ammo build to weapons loading to the actual launching or dropping of the weapons from the aircraft. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Master Sgt. Carl Clegg)

gallery.title: File:Emergency Medical Procedure Training (14003051022).jpg
gallery.artist: Georgia National Guard from United States
gallery.description:
TYNDALL AIR FORCE BASE, April 17, 2014 -  Technical Sgt. Barry Duffield, left, an explosive ordnance disposal  technician with the 116th Civil Engineering Squadron, Georgia Air National Guard, Robins Air Force Base, Ga., and Tech. Sgt. Dustin Turner, an EOD technician with the 123rd Airlift Wing, Kentucky ANG, Louisville, Ky., attempt to stop bleeding from the leg of a Multiple Amputation Trauma Trainer during Silver Flag training.
During the weeklong course, Guardsmen from the 116th CES along with 219 Airmen from multiple U.S. Air Force active duty, Reserve and Air National Guard units trained on building and maintaining bare-base operations at a simulated forward-deployed location. In addition, they honed their combat and survival skills, repaired simulated bomb-damaged runways, practiced EOD scenarios, set up base facilities and established various critical base operating support capabilities. Thirty-four Airmen from the 116th CES attended the exercise that consisted of extensive classroom and hands-on training culminating in an evaluation of learned skills on the last day of class. 

(U.S. Air National Guard photo by Master Sgt. Roger Parsons/Released)
